Introduction

This Nuclear Waste Services Topic Manual (NWSTM) forms part of the Quality Section of the Nuclear Waste Services Integrated Management System (IMS).

As a guiding manual it outlines the expectations and interactions between the customer and the contract in the context of the oversight of quality assurance activities, for which a detailed but not exhausted list can be found in appendix 3 - typical oversight & Assurance activities.

Nuclear Waste Services and its regulators reserve the right to undertake oversight of the contractor management system arrangements and all work being delivered within the contract scope including sub-contractor work. Oversight may by delivered means of assessment, inspection, verification, surveillance or formal audit. The contractor shall suitably inform their respective sub-contractors appropriately of this requirement as part of their flow down arrangements.

A range of documents may be referenced throughout as a guiding/more detailed principle, however the key relating NWS process to this manual is NWSSOP 08.09 (How do we deliver quality in a Project environment) which can be used intelligently applied across all work scopes to help satisfy the expectations set out within this document

For any clarification on the range of terminology used throughout this manual, a glossary has been created within appendix 1 of the document.

Aims

This document aims to ensure the safe and predictable delivery of projects, products and services through quality control, assurance, verification and validation of activities.

It extends to all tier of the supply chain via standard “flow down” arrangements. Flow-down is the dissemination of the Nuclear Waste Services quality arrangements established for the specified Assurance grading and/or Specification. These arrangements shall be adopted regardless of the Contractors operational location(s).

Purpose

Quality standards aim to support the delivery of excellence in all aspects of services, operating safely, securely, reliably and predictably. To achieve this aim, it is a requirement for the Supply Chain to deliver the quality of Projects, Products and Services safely, to schedule, to the specified requirements and to the agreed cost.

The purpose of this documents scope is to define the Contract Quality Requirements that will enable the delivery of Projects, Products and Services to the applicable Assurance grade. It is important to recognise that this document is intended to supplement an already implemented Quality Management System in line with BS EN ISO 9001:2015, however this document focuses on the NWS elements not specifically within that standard which over time have proved key to successful delivery of Projects, Products and Services to specified quality requirements.

In the event that any inconsistencies present themselves between this document and the contact between NWS and the contractor, the legally binding contract shall take precedence.

The oversight arrangements, Contract Quality Requirements and performance metrics detailed in the document reflect the key principles and activities that promote Quality control, assurance, verification and validation of projects, products and services within the Nuclear Waste Services supply chain. These oversight and assurance arrangements are designed to minimize the risk of non-conformance, defects and Counterfeit, Fraudulent and Suspect items (CFSI).

This may include but is not limited to the following;

Identifying and managing identified risks within the Supply chain

Principles for establishing risk based approach to contractor oversight

Qualifications of suitably qualified and experience persons (SQEP)

Projects, Products and Services

This document is designed to encompass and be intelligently applied at all phases of contract delivery by the NWS supply chain as shown below and also within Appendix 3: Typical oversight and assurance activities.

NWSSOP 08.09 (How do we deliver quality in a Project environment) details an NWS approach to structure how a PDCA (plan, do, check, act) cycle alongside useful guidance on roles, responsibilities and key tasks which contribute to successful delivery of projects, products and services.

This diagram(s) within NWSSOP 8.09 details where oversight and assurance arrangements for all projects, products and services supplied to nuclear waste services as determined by the EHSSQ assurance grade and associated product specification(s)/regulatory requirements.

Flow Down

The contractor shall comply with all the requirements as applicable to the specified Project, Product or service as defined in the contractual document and ensure the requirements are flowed to every applicable tier of the supply chain.

Supply Chain Tier

Designation of EHSSQ Assurance Grading

Dependant on the Assurance grade selected for a product or service, the colour coding at the heading at particular sections of this document will determine if those requirements are applicable. These are identified where deemed applicable using the key shown to the right of each heading. For example, (as below) if all of the specified grades are coloured green, this indicates that all clauses within the heading shall apply to the scope of works.

In cases where the Assurance grade is shown as pale green, then such requirements are by exception/agreement, however it is noted that such agreements shall be specifically stated as a requirement within the contractual scope document or supporting works information and shall always take precedence in any such discrepancies.

Guiding Principles/Concepts

The following principles underpin the successful application of oversight and assurance of quality management systems arrangements within Nuclear Waste Services supply chain and customers and contractors shall act in accordance with these principles at all times.

Nuclear Waste Services will act as the Intelligent Customer regarding application of this document

shall provide NWS with copies of their management review records relevant to the Contract work scope.

The Contractor shall notify NWS of any management review actions which have or potentially could affect compliance with contractual requirements.

Where organisational changes to the Contractors’ Quality Management System could present potential loss of certification(s) or an acceptable level of project delivery, product or services this shall be brought to the attention of Nuclear Waste Services for acceptance/approval. Acceptance/approval may be withheld if in the opinion of Nuclear Waste Services, the quality management system arrangements present a risk or do no longer comply with any specific obligations within the agreed contract(s) in place.

Contract Placement Phase

Resource Management

Modern Slavery Act (MSA) 2015

Contractors shall implement a Code of Conduct with specific focus on modern slavery issues including appropriate contractor control, oversight, and assurance mechanisms

The Contractor shall implement an induction course to include the full scope of works.

The Contractor shall ensure that all designated personnel deployed on NWS’ work scope receive an induction course prior to commencing work on the contract. The induction course shall as a minimum include:

Nuclear Safety Awareness

Conventional Safety requirements

Applicable Security requirements

Overview of the work scope

Mandatory procedures

Requirement briefs against all Standards and Specifications relevant to the work scope.

Applying effective oversight upon Project delivery, products and services utilizes SQEP (Suitably Qualified and Experienced Persons). To be considered as SQEP, individuals’ professional competence shall be demonstrated and traceable to a competency matrix linked to their role. Professional competence is deemed to be demonstrable knowledge, skills and experience as appropriate to the task or activity being undertaken and shall be supported by formal training and qualification(s) (national / international). Evidence of scheduled Periodic Reviews shall be maintained and Forward Planning to close out identified competencies or progress of working toward upskilling/training requirements.

The Contractor shall notify NWS in writing of any deficiencies identified with personnel competency that may affect the item or service provided, in a timely manner. The Contractor shall take timely corrective actions and communicate these to NWS.

The Contractor shall be able to demonstrate the qualification and independence of Personnel verifying or inspecting work from those performing the work. NWS reserves the right to interview these personnel to determine this as required.

Procurement

Graded Approach to Procurement

NWS implements a graded approach to the procurement of Projects, Products and Services within the supply chain via NWSSOP 8.05. This graded approach ensures that the appropriate levels of assurance and oversight are deployed, commensurate with the level of risk.

The contractor shall also apply a considered graded approach to procurement, deploying resources on consideration of:

The magnitude of potential consequences if an item fails or an activity is carried out incorrectly

The significance and complexity of each item or activity

The hazards and the magnitude of the potential impact (risks) that are associated to the safety, environmental, security, quality and economic elements of each item or activity.

NWS EHSSQ Assurance grade(s) selected as 01 and 02 will require mandatory NWS oversight and assurance activities at the Contractor’s/sub-contractor’s works or the specific location(s) where inspection or testing is taking place. This shall require submission of controlling documents such as Quality Plans, Inspection and Test plans or written method statements to the requirements stipulated within the contract specifications. Upon completion, work will require a certificate of conformity and a final inspection release certification by an NWS inspection representative. Quality Grade 01/02 items will generally require a lifetime record (LTR) pack which will also require verification and endorsement by NWS as part of the agreed handover arrangements.

NWS utilises one additional Assurance Grade that may be applicable for the direct supply of item to Nuclear Waste Services Ltd. Grade 02P (P - Proprietary) is utilised for the procurement of proprietary spares and equipment deemed high risk (i.e. typically catalogue items) but from a source of proven capability. The NWS Assurance grading risk process may identify a high risk; however, the contractor shall be compliant with Quality Grade 03 requirements but may need to supply additional supporting information dependant on the nature of the product.

Graded 03 Projects, products and Services will require goods receipt inspection by NWS as a minimum. Manufacturer’s Certificates of Conformance and supporting information depending on the nature of the product will be required as stipulated within the purchasing information. By exception, Quality Plans may be requested by NWS in some instances. Quality Plan usage at QG03 shall then require surveillances and reviews by NWS SQEP personnel as detailed within the agreed controlling document.

If the Project, Product or Service being procured can be demonstrated to carry low/no risk, then a Quality Grade 04 may be applied by NWS and therefore the requirements of this document will be intelligently applied to the relevant contractor. Assurance Grade 04 should only be used for items that, if failed on delivery or utilisation would have Low to No implications regarding Nuclear/Radiological safety, Conventional safety, Environmental impact, or Business risk.

Inspection checklists and associated contractor inspection and test plans shall be utilized to control the release and acceptance of construction works on site.

Correction Fluid such as ‘Tippex’ or similar is not to be used. Any mistakes to be corrected shall be done by a single strike through line so that the previous information can still be read. The amendment shall then be signed, stamped and dated at the side of the change(s) made.

The agreed number of sets of the Lifetime Records shall be, unless stated otherwise in the contracts, be sent to the applicable Project Quality Engineer/Lead for the contract as identified at the opening meeting.

Preservation of Items including delivery and receipt

Contractors are expected to inform NWS of specific requirements and processes that are necessary for the ongoing maintenance and preservation of item(s) before and during use. Operations and maintenance manuals may form part of the deliverables within the contractual agreements.

Contractors bringing chemicals on to NWS property are reminded that permission and a CoSHH assessment is required before the goods are brought on to site.

Contractors holding stock for NWS are reminded that this stock shall be segregated from their own incoming stores items.

Indoor spares storage areas shall be clean and dry with no potential for condensation. Storage temperatures shall be between 5°C and 25°C.

Perishable sealing items shall be stored using the principles of BS ISO 2230 Rubber products, Guidance for storage.

If no NWS or agreed contractor specification exists chemicals and paints shall be stored according to the CoSHH assessment and the Manufacturer’s recommendations.

Care shall be taken to control surface contact of incompatible materials and items, and incompatible storage of chemicals.

Cross contamination of stainless-steel items shall be prevented by appropriate segregation from other non-stainless steel, metal objects or fixings.

The Contractor should ensure the security of item and its constituent parts during internal processing and delivery to NWS.

The Contractor is responsible for establishing a specified storage area, on NWS site Contracts this will be provided by the Construction Manager. The storage area must satisfy the relevant requirements of the contractual Specifications and must be maintained to agreed standards. The specified storage area shall contain a secure and dedicated quarantine area.

Related Documentation

Methods of accessing NWS controlled documents within the Integrated management will be discussed and detailed in the contract. To ensure version control and updates to relevant NWS with regard to access and review of documentation, these can be made available by NWS at request. It is important to note that if a specific revision of a document is referenced within a contract, the revision stated shall take precedence.

Relevant Compliance

This document has been generated with consideration of relevant health and safety legislation. Where appropriate legislation has been referenced, however, the primary legislation that has influence in this document is:

Office for Nuclear Regulation – Licence Condition Handbook

Office for Nuclear Regulation – Technical Assessment Guide (TAG 077)

Internal Atomic Energy Agency – Safety Standards

Abbreviations

Summary of key abbreviations used in this document:

Audit Systematic, independent and documented process for obtaining audit evidence and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which audit criteria are fulfilled

Assessment Process for analysing a contractor’s competencies, facilities and equipment to provide confidence in the capability to conform to the Contract requirements, delivering items and services safely, to schedule, of the correct quality and to cost

Assurance A systematic approach to confirm activities are being completed as per the requirements, to the appropriate standard and to confirm that arrangements comply with required legislation, standards and NWS Repository Ltd requirements

Concessions Permission to use or release of item or service that does not conform to requirements

Contractor/Sub-Contractor Supplier or individual who provides items or services in accordance with NWS Contract requirements. Contractor is an all-inclusive term which may be used in place of: supplier, Contractor, Sub-Contractor or consultant

Counterfeit Items intentionally manufactured or altered to imitate a legitimate item in order to pass themselves off as genuine

Deviation Departures from the originally specified requirements of an item prior to realisation. Deviations can emerge at any stage of the Supply Chain, including design, manufacturing, storage and transportation.

Flow-down Distribution of NWS Contract requirements as applicable to the specified Quality Grade to every tier of the Supply Chain where the risk associated with the procurement of item or services continues to be a grading of 01, 02, 03 0r 04

Foreign Material Exclusion (FME) The process of preventing the introduction of outside debris into an area or areas where that debris poses an economic risk or safety hazard.

Fraudulent Fraudulent items are misrepresented with intent to deceive, including items with incorrect identification or false certifications.

Hold Point Hold Point is a mandatory verification point beyond which a work cannot proceed without approval by the Engineer / Inspector. The work cannot proceed until the Engineer / Inspector is able to verify the quality of the completed work and releases the Hold by means of Inspection Request approval.

Inspector The independent body or organisation that verifies that items or services have been designed, constructed, and tested in accordance with the technical Specification.
